doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Stopping the show against Thelma Carpenter and Teddy Wilson
summary: In 1954-55 she played a $500 engagement against Thelma Carpenter and Teddy Wilson, stole the show, and Carpenter never spoke to her again.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: At what point in your career where you able to close it?
When I appeared against Teddy Wilson and Thelma Carpenter.

’54.’55. George Gewee (?) said I called and asked for the job, you know. So, he gave me $500, I said, “Oh, I’ll make this due.” He said, “Oh, you gotta pay your men out of it.” I said, “That’s alright too.” So, I played against Thelma Carpenter and Teddy Wilson. And Thelma
Carpenter took all the time. I said, “You can take all night, it ain’t gonna make no difference.” So I got on there and stopped that show cold.
What happened after you stole the show?
She never spoke to me again. She said, “Dorothy stole the show but I closed it.” I said, “Closed it?” Yeah.
